products.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A large portion of central North Carolina, including the
following counties, Alamance, Chatham, Cumberland, Durham,
Edgecombe, Forsyth, Franklin, Granville, Guilford, Halifax,
Harnett, Hoke, Johnston, Lee, Moore, Nash, Orange, Person,
Randolph, Sampson, Vance, Wake, Warren, Wayne and Wilson.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A vigorous storm system with anomalous moisture and strong lift
will cause rain to expand and become moderate to heavy tonight
into Thursday morning. A broad area of 2 to 5 inches is expected,
with localized higher amounts between 5 and 8 inches possible in
the Coastal Plain and adjacent eastern Piedmont and Sandhills.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
products.headline: Flood Watch issued November 26 at 1:22AM EST until November 26 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Raleigh NC
products.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

products.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts between 35 and 45
mph.

* WHERE...All of central North Carolina.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
damage, including downed limbs and a risk of some uprooted trees in
saturated soil overnight, may result in scattered power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Isolated gusts to near 50 mph will be possible
into the early morning hours, especially during times of heaviest
rain.
products.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 26 at 1:25AM EST until November 26 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Raleigh NC
products.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

products.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Chatham County in central North Carolina...
Northeastern Cumberland County in central North Carolina...
Durham County in central North Carolina...
Edgecombe County in central North Carolina...
Franklin County in central North Carolina...
Southeastern Granville County in central North Carolina...
Halifax County in central North Carolina...
Northeastern Harnett County in central North Carolina...
Johnston County in central North Carolina...
Nash County in central North Carolina...
Southeastern Orange County in central North Carolina...
Sampson County in central North Carolina...
Wake County in central North Carolina...
Warren County in central North Carolina...
Wayne County in central North Carolina...
Wilson County in central North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 845 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 239 AM EST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 4
inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 4 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Raleigh, Durham, Cary, Rocky Mount, Chapel Hill, Goldsboro,
Roanoke Rapids, Tarboro, Smithfield, Clinton, Hillsborough,
Nashville, Mount Olive, Creedmoor, Louisburg, Lillington,
Warrenton, Halifax, Wilson and Wake Forest.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
products.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 2:39AM EST until November 26 at 8:45AM EST by NWS Raleigh NC
products.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
